An older translation is not evidence about the source, and I had four days of translations agreeing with each other.

value: (a) The band becomes AUTHORED rather than stamped — hand-numbering back under a new name, inserting a sieve becomes a write to its neighbours (Law 6), and ruling 2026-08-06 has been quietly reversed. THE TELL: someone hand-edits a declaration.
(b) The reconciler AUTO-RESTAMPS on mismatch — the check can then never fail, which is the check that goes green for the wrong reason.
(c) The reconciler NEVER fires a mismatch across real use (ceremony) or fires constantly (noise, which gets trained away while still looking like coverage).
(d) A declaration is written that NOTHING READS — the half-built state where the data exists and the consumers still walk the AST. Strictly worse than today, because then there are two answers.

value.recorded_as: a distinction, not a collision — with the tell named above so a later reader can see it arrive if it does.
value.the_shape_of_the_answer: Persisted-but-derived is a THIRD option neither ruling considered. Derived-only (today) is unreadable; authored (killed) goes stale and writes neighbours; stamped-and-reconciled is readable, cannot be authored, and cannot silently drift.
value.what_that_ruling_killed: Hand-numbering the sieves, for two named defects (inspector.py's own comment): inserting a check 'would make inserting one a WRITE TO ITS NEIGHBOURS (Law 6)', and a derived band — unlike an authored one — 'cannot go stale'.
value.why_a_stamped_band_carries_neither: The value is STAMPED FROM THE DERIVATION, never authored. Inserting a sieve writes that sieve's own declaration and no other, so there are no neighbour-writes. And staleness is precisely what the reconciler exists to catch, at the declared polarity.

value: WHERE THE DECLARATION LIVES, exactly. 'Attached to the sieve' is unambiguous about the RELATION and silent about the ADDRESS. A sieve today is a module-level Python function with a docstring; candidates are a sibling JSON file, a structured block in the docstring, or a decorator. The docstring option has precedent (the Provenance line lives there) and a strike against it: parsing prose for a number is the mention-not-capability failure sieve.py's own header records twice.
WHAT THE RECONCILER DOES ON A MISMATCH. Polarity is settled; the ACT is not. Red the build gate, raise a trouble, or report? Auto-restamp is NOT a free choice — it is wrong-intent (b).

DOES THE LADDER'S VERSION RIDE THE STAMP? Akien, 2026-08-11: a sieve 'is the best effort and will learn from experience.' The learning is not on the sieve's verdict (a rule is true or not) — it is on DEFAULT_LADDER, which its own comment calls 'a first cut (2026-08-06), not a settled taxonomy... Widening it is expected.' So a mismatch has TWO possible causes, needing opposite responses: the sieve's body moved (that declaration is stale, restamp it) or the LADDER moved (every declaration in the corpus is now off, and nothing is stale — the measure changed). Without a ladder version on the stamp those are indistinguishable, and a ladder widening reads as N stale sieves. A chart question, not a cast one.
DOES nest() CHANGE? Believed no (see measured_at_cast). If yes, cairn/tools/base/nest.py joins the ruling's what_conforms and the file list was short by one.

value.the_code_already_assumed_it: reach_of's transitivity follows BARE-NAME calls only (sieve.py:173, isinstance(node.func, ast.Name)) — precisely how module-level functions call each other. The walk was never a partial view of a wider world; it was the whole world, correctly walked.
value.the_rule: A SIEVE IS A MODULE-LEVEL FUNCTION. Not a convention the walker must tolerate exceptions to — the shape of the thing.
value.verbatim: a seive is a rule. it is true or not. it's the best effort and will learn from experience. why could it not be a function?
value.what_it_replaced: CC had flagged as a HOLE that reach_of walks module-level FunctionDef nodes only, so a sieve written as a method, a closure, or as data would silently receive band 0 — and had argued this got worse once the band was persisted. Measured after the ruling: ZERO such sieves exist (39 module-level functions and no classes in inspector.py; 11 plus one exception class in route.py). CC was proposing to widen the walker to shapes nothing uses — designing for complexity, walking past the simpler answer.
value.what_this_buys_at_no_extra_cost: The declaration this ticket builds IS the roster, so the rule becomes checkable by the reconciler already in scope: every declared sieve must resolve to a module-level function in its own module. Resolving to a method, a closure, or to nothing is LOUD — not band 0. A hypothetical hole becomes a real check (Law 4), for one more comparison rather than a new mechanism.

value.cc_recommendation_not_a_ruling: This should land BEFORE a-gate-is-a-class, not inside it.
value.what_the_other_order_costs: The gate work would be inventing the declaration format and the reconciler at the same time as the gate class, with nothing proven underneath.
value.what_this_order_costs: The declaration needs an interim home, because the gate seed folder does not exist yet, and the gate work later migrates it. A known, bounded migration rather than an unknown design risk.
value.why: It is small, bounded by three measured files, its acceptance test already exists as a door, and it proves the stamp-and-reconcile pattern — including the polarity question — on real code before the gate build depends on that pattern working for six gates at once. Solidify the layer below.
